title: Short and long time horizons

blocks.heading: Short and long time horizons
blocks.text: Short-term planning concerns nearer actions and resource decisions. Long-term planning sets a direction and intended outcomes over a longer horizon. Their distinction is relative to the context; there is no universal number of years that fits every organisation or activity. A long-term aim to improve access to skilled work can involve shorter actions such as recruiting tutors, arranging transport or repairing a training room. These actions form a route towards the wider goal. They must be relevant to the barrier identified, not merely convenient to count.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Stages should connect
blocks.text: Consider an invented district aiming to widen training access over several years. For the next term, it schedules a serviceable vehicle, driver and route to communities with the longest journeys. That near-term action is specific enough to implement. The longer direction is wider access and improved capabilities. Monitoring attendance and completion tests whether the transport action contributes to that direction. If missing childcare rather than distance remains the main barrier, the route may need revision or a complementary response. Changing a practical action in light of evidence can support the long-term aim rather than abandon it.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: A dated national example: NDP5
blocks.text: Namibia's Fifth National Development Plan, NDP5, covered 2017/18–2021/22. Use it here as a historical example. Its stated goals addressed inclusive and equitable economic growth, people's capabilities and health, environmental protection and resilience, and governance through effective institutions. These goals connect economic progress with social conditions, resources and public implementation. They are intended directions; listing them does not establish what was achieved. The National Planning Commission's [NDP5 summary](https://www.npc.gov.na/national-plans/national-plans-ndp-5/) records the period and goal indicators, checked for this lesson on 20 October 2026. Its target columns must be read as targets, not observed results.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: How to evaluate the example
blocks.text: Begin with one stated goal, then identify evidence that would show progress towards it. For a human-capabilities goal, facility construction is relevant implementation evidence, but service access, quality or usable skills are closer to the intended outcome. Compare a baseline and later observation measured consistently. Ask whether progress reaches the relevant groups and whether the supporting resources can be maintained. A positive change may have several causes, so avoid attributing the whole change to a plan without evidence. Equally, an unmet target is not evidence that every action had no benefit. An evaluation should distinguish progress, remaining gaps and the limits of the evidence.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: An original evaluation case
blocks.text: The following is fictional practice and is not a claim about NDP5 performance. A programme aims to increase training access in remote settlements. It meets a target of opening four centres. However, only one has regular tutors and attendance remains unchanged. Judged by buildings, implementation appears successful; judged by usable training access, the result is limited. Assigning tutors and monitoring actual attendance would address the gap more directly than opening a fifth centre. The judgement follows the stated access criterion and uses both construction and service evidence. It is stronger than declaring the whole programme successful because one target was met.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Keep policy examples dated
blocks.text: Vision 2030 in Topic 2.1 gives the longer context; health and education in Topics 7.2 and 7.3 explain some intended benefits. When evaluating NDP5, name its period and goals, then separate real source evidence from an illustrative scenario. This lesson does not claim a final national verdict or describe NDP5 as the current programme.
